data: Welcome to Dapp-Forge - A fully decentralized exchange (DEX) platform built on Ethereum blockchain technology.
data.-what-is-dapp-forge#🎯 What is Dapp-Forge: Dapp-Forge is a decentralized application (DApp) that enables peer-to-peer token trading without intermediaries. Built on Ethereum smart contracts, it provides a trustless, transparent, and secure platform for exchanging ERC-20 tokens with ETH.
data.key-features#Key Features:
🔒 Trustless Trading - No intermediaries, trade directly with other users
🌐 Transparent - All transactions recorded on blockchain
💰 Non-Custodial - You control your assets at all times
⚡ Real-time - Live order books and instant trade execution
📊 Professional Charts - ApexCharts integration for price visualization
🔐 Secure - Auditable smart contracts with safety mechanisms
data.-quick-start#🚀 Quick Start:
Get started in 5 minutes:
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Hrsh111/Dapp-Forge.git
# 2. Navigate to client directory
cd Dapp-Forge/client
# 3. Install dependencies
npm install
# 4. Start development server
npm start
The app will open at http://localhost:3000

data.decentralized-exchange-dex#Decentralized:
Unlike centralized exchanges (like Coinbase), Dapp-Forge:
Non-custodial: You control your private keys
Trustless: No need to trust a third party
Transparent: All transactions on blockchain
Censorship-resistant: No one can block your trades
data.order-book-model#Order Book Model:
Dapp-Forge uses an on-chain order book:
Makers: Users who create orders (provide liquidity)
Takers: Users who fill existing orders
Limit Orders: Orders executed at specific price or better
Instant Settlement: Trades settle immediately on-chain

Event emission for UI updates
Fee mechanism (configurable)

data: Complete technical documentation for the Exchange.sol smart contract - the core of Dapp-Forge's decentralized trading system.
data.-contract-overview#📋 Contract Overview: The Exchange contract is a decentralized exchange (DEX) that allows users to trade ERC-20 tokens and ETH in a trustless manner using an on-chain order book model.
data.contract-details#Contract Details:
Language: Solidity ^0.8.0
License: MIT
Model: Order Book DEX
Settlement: Instant on-chain
data.order-structure#Order Structure:
struct _Order {
    uint256 id;              // Unique order identifier
    address user;            // Address of order creator
    address tokenGet;        // Token user wants to receive
    uint256 amountGet;       // Amount user wants to receive
    address tokenGive;       // Token user is giving
    uint256 amountGive;      // Amount user is giving
    uint256 timestamp;       // When order was created
}
Understanding the Order Structure:
For a buy order: tokenGet = DAPP, tokenGive = ETH
For a sell order: tokenGet = ETH, tokenGive = DAPP
Price = amountGive / amountGet
data.makeorder#makeOrder():
function makeOrder(
    address _tokenGet, 
    uint256 _amountGet, 
    address _tokenGive, 
    uint256 _amountGive
) public {
    require(balanceOf(_tokenGive, msg.sender) >= _amountGive);
    
    orderCount = orderCount + 1;
    orders[orderCount] = _Order(
        orderCount,
        msg.sender,
        _tokenGet,
        _amountGet,
        _tokenGive,
        _amountGive,
        block.timestamp
    );
    
    emit Order(orderCount, msg.sender, _tokenGet, _amountGet, 
        _tokenGive, _amountGive, block.timestamp);
}
How it works:
Validates user has sufficient balance
Increments order counter
Creates new order in storage
Emits Order event
Parameters Explained:
_tokenGet: What you want to receive
_amountGet: How much you want to receive
_tokenGive: What you're offering
_amountGive: How much you're offering
Example: Buy Order
// Buy 100 DAPP for 10 ETH
// Price: 0.1 ETH per DAPP
await exchange.methods.makeOrder(
  dappToken.address,                    // tokenGet: DAPP
  web3.utils.toWei('100', 'ether'),     // amountGet: 100 DAPP
  ETHER_ADDRESS,                        // tokenGive: ETH
  web3.utils.toWei('10', 'ether')       // amountGive: 10 ETH
).send({ from: buyer })
Example: Sell Order
// Sell 100 DAPP for 10 ETH
// Price: 0.1 ETH per DAPP
await exchange.methods.makeOrder(
  ETHER_ADDRESS,                        // tokenGet: ETH
  web3.utils.toWei('10', 'ether'),      // amountGet: 10 ETH
  dappToken.address,                    // tokenGive: DAPP
  web3.utils.toWei('100', 'ether')      // amountGive: 100 DAPP
).send({ from: seller })
Requirements:
Must have deposited sufficient balance
All amounts must be > 0
Gas Cost: ~100,000 gas

Current Status:
⚠️ Susceptible to front-running (common in order book DEXs)Potential Mitigations:

data: Complete technical documentation for the Token.sol smart contract - the ERC-20 token implementation used in Dapp-Forge.
data.-contract-overview#📋 Contract Overview: The Token contract is a standard ERC-20 token implementation that provides the basic functionality for creating, transferring, and managing fungible tokens on the Ethereum blockchain.
data.contract-details#Contract Details:
Standard: ERC-20
Language: Solidity ^0.8.0
License: MIT
Decimals: 18 (standard)
data.what-is-erc-20#What is ERC-20?:
ERC-20 is the technical standard for fungible tokens on Ethereum. "Fungible" means each token is identical and interchangeable (like dollars or bitcoins).Key characteristics:
✅ Standardized interface
✅ Compatible with all ERC-20 wallets and exchanges
✅ Well-tested and battle-proven
✅ Wide ecosystem support
data.state-variables#State Variables:
string public name;                          // Token name (e.g., "Dapp Token")
string public symbol;                        // Token symbol (e.g., "DAPP")
uint256 public decimals = 18;                // Decimal places (standard: 18)
uint256 public totalSupply;                  // Total tokens in existence
mapping(address => uint256) public balanceOf;                     // User balances
mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public allowance; // Spending approvals
data.transfer-function#Transfer Function:
function transfer(address _to, uint256 _value) 
    public returns (bool success) {
    require(balanceOf[msg.sender] >= _value);
    _transfer(msg.sender, _to, _value);
    return true;
}
How it works:
Checks sender has sufficient balance
Calls internal _transfer function
Returns true on success
Usage:
// Send 100 tokens to another address
await token.methods.transfer(
  recipientAddress,
  web3.utils.toWei('100', 'ether')
).send({ from: senderAddress })
What happens:
Before:
sender: 1000 tokens
recipient: 500 tokens
After:
sender: 900 tokens
recipient: 600 tokens
Requirements:
Sender must have >= _value tokens
_to address must not be 0x0
_value must be > 0
Gas Cost: ~50,000 gas
data.what-are-decimals#What are decimals?:
Tokens have no fractional values in smart contracts. Instead, we use decimals to represent fractions:
Decimals: 18 (standard for ERC-20)
Human-readable: 1.5 tokens
Contract value:  1500000000000000000 wei
Human-readable: 0.001 tokens
Contract value:  1000000000000000 wei
data.why-18-decimals#Why 18 decimals?:
Matches ETH's decimals
Allows for very small fractions
Standard across most tokens
Compatible with exchanges
data.zero-address-checks#Zero Address Checks:
require(_to != address(0));
Why important:
Sending to 0x0 burns tokens (unrecoverable)
Common mistake by users
Protection against accidents
data.balance-validation#Balance Validation:
require(balanceOf[msg.sender] >= _value);
Prevents:
Spending more than you have
Negative balances
Unauthorized transfers
data.allowance-checks#Allowance Checks:
require(_value <= allowance[_from][msg.sender]);
Prevents:
Spending more than approved
Unauthorized transferFrom calls
Allowance exploitation
